newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia retains trade deficit with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia retains trade deficit with Turkey.

text.p: Macedonia ran a $13.8 million trade deficit with Turkey during January-July 1996, the Skopje daily Nova Makedonija reported on Monday.
Macedonia's seven-month imports from Turkey totalled $24.3 million while exports stood at $10.5 million, the paper said, quoting official statistics.
Trade between Macedonia and Turkey reached $93.5 million in 1995, with Macedonian exports accounting for $38.6 million and imports for $54.9 million, the paper said.
"Neither we nor our Turkish partners pleased with these results," a Macedonian businessman, who attended a meeting of Macedonian and Turkish businessmen in Ohrid last week, told Reuters.
Businessmen argued that neither governments have done anything to ease the trade between the two countries.
They also insisted on raising bilateral cooperation to a much higher level.

"We want our governments to simplify and finalise all legal provisions to really implement the principle of the most-favoured nation, which is part of the agreement on trade and economic cooperation signed between Macedonia and Turkey two years ago," said the businessman who declined to be named.
Due to customs and standards barriers, bilateral trade is scaled down to "petty trade" by-passing legal channels and bringing products of dubious quality into the country, the businessman said.
According to official statistics, there are 200 mixed Macedonian-Turkish trade companies in Macedonia.

Currently, Macedonia expects to cash in the approved $25 million commodity credit from the Turkish Exim Bank and an establishment of a mixed Macedonian-Turkish bank, to promote bilateral trade. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom, +389 91 201 196
